svg.title: Transactional outbox
svg.desc: Commit the event with the data in one transaction; a relay publishes it later. The relay publishes, then marks the row sent. A crash between the two re-publishes the event, so delivery is at-least-once and consumers must be idempotent. Consumers downstream of the broker are not drawn. Polling is shown; log-tailing CDC (e.g. Debezium) is an equivalent relay. 1. Atomic write: order row and outbox event commit in one transaction. 2. Relay polls: relay reads the pending event from the outbox table. 3. Broker down: publish fails, so the row stays pending. 4. Retry succeeds: after a backoff the relay retries and the broker acks. 5. Marked sent: only after the ack does the relay mark the row sent.
